text:
Tampa Bay out-attempted the Rangers 57 to 43 and finished with the slightly higher expected goals total (2.66 to 2.54), yet New York walked out of Madison Square Garden with a 4-1 win. By the simulation, TBL deserved to win 53 percent of the time. Nothing in the data suggests the Rangers were dominated, only that the chances fell their way.

The first period explains most of it. Alexis Lafrenière scored at 1:02 on a 19 percent chance, then again at 12:47 on a 2 percent chance, the least likely goal of the night, both with Tye Kartye assisting. Zemgus Girgensons cut it to 2-1 at 17:26, and Tampa Bay carried the second period, outpacing New York 1.14 to 0.85 in expected goals. Will Cuylle tipped in a 3-1 goal with 1:34 left in that period on an 8 percent look, and the push produced nothing more.

Dylan Garand did the rest, stopping 25 of 26 shots and saving 1.66 goals more than the quality of those shots deserved. Andrei Vasilevskiy allowed three on 22 shots, 0.5 goals worse than expected, including a 28 percent first-period chance from Mika Zibanejad. Zibanejad did score late, a shorthanded wrist shot at 17:16 of the third on a 3 percent chance, to close it out. Both power plays went 0 for 4, and New York won the faceoff count 33 to 21 and the hit count 37 to 22. It was the second win over Tampa Bay this season, after a 5-1 result on October 1.
